titleZh: 酒店团队集中抵店，怎样安排入住才能少排队？
titleEn: Hotel Group Arrivals: How Can Check-in Be Organised to Reduce Queues?
summaryZh: 通过小程序预登记、在途确认、房态与结算核对及异常分流，减少团队抵店后的重复办理与等待；附接待核对字段、责任分工和验证方法。
summaryEn: Coordinate preregistration, on-the-way updates, room readiness, payment arrangements and exception handling to reduce duplicated work and waiting during group arrivals.
contentZh:
酒店团队集中抵店，怎样安排入住才能少排队？

酒店团队集中抵店，要减少排队，可通过小程序等渠道提前完成适用的预登记，把抵店批次、分房名单、可交付房态和结算安排核对清楚，再把异常交给专人处理；如果卡在房间尚未准备好，增加前台人手也不能缩短等房时间。

团队接待的准备工作，不能只看预订了多少间房。销售掌握的抵店时间、客房部预计完成的清洁时间和前厅准备发出的房卡，必须对应同一批客人。否则，看似资料齐全，客人到了仍要重新问姓名、找房间、确认谁付押金。

展会换展和会议报到等节点尤其值得提前核对。商务部公布的第140届广交会排期中，第二期为2026年10月23日至27日。这是接待准备的时间提醒，并不说明所有周边酒店都有团队入住。酒店应以已经确认的订单和到店信息安排人员，不能把展会规模直接换算成自己的接待量。

## 先分清客人是在等手续，还是在等房间

一批客人在大堂等待，背后可能是两类问题。一类是可以入住，却因名单变更、结算不明或反复找订单，迟迟办不完手续；另一类是手续已经办好，但客房尚未清洁、检查或解除维修状态。

前一类应减少现场核对和返工，后一类则要协调房间交付顺序、等候安排及信息告知。把两类等待混在一起统计，很容易让前厅以为必须再开柜台，也让客房部误以为客人还没有办好手续。

准备会应同时看预计抵店人数和届时真正可以交付的房间。提前分配房号只是计划；房间可交付，才具备发放入住凭证的条件。不能为了让系统显示处理完成，就把未准备好的房间交给客人。

## 把名单、房态与结算核对放到抵店前

销售或团队联络人先确认预计抵店批次、各批人数、房型需求和团方联系人。整团乘车抵达与参会者自行分批到店，接待安排不同。时间不确定时要保留预计区间，并约定由谁更新；不能把最初报价时的到店时间一直沿用到接待当天。

前厅据此核对名单和订单，包括同住关系、不同入住日期、提前到店及临时延住等会影响分房的信息。每份名单标明更新时间和维护人，变更统一回到负责核对的人员手中，避免销售、领队和柜台各持一份不同版本。

客房部提供的应是按抵店批次可交付的房间，而不只是当天计划清洁的总量。前厅需要知道哪些房间已经可以交付，哪些仍待处理，以及下一次更新时间。提前做好房卡或卡套的，也必须在实际交付时核对客人和房号，名单变更后同步处理。

结算则由销售与财务提前确认：哪些费用由团方承担，哪些由住客自付，押金或担保如何办理，临时加房和升级由谁批准。前厅应能查到已确认的安排，不必每接待一位客人就重新打电话询问。未明确的费用不能被“整个团队统一结算”这句话掩盖。

Oracle的OPERA Cloud官方说明将预登记、分房与批量入住分别处理，并为批量入住设置到店状态、付款信息和房间占用状态等前提。这说明系统提速依赖前置条件，不是选中一批订单就能解决所有问题。具体功能随系统版本与配置而异，酒店不需要为了采用这套方法先更换系统。

提前准备不等于提前完成身份核验。《旅馆业治安管理办法》第六条要求接待住宿登记时查验身份证件并如实登记。领队提供名单不能代替酒店按规定完成的查验与登记；具体手续还应符合所在地现行要求。接待准备表只记录协调所需信息，避免把证件号码等资料复制到无关人员都能看到的工作群或公开展示板上。

## 把Pre-check-in延伸到客人抵店途中

Pre-check-in的价值，是让适合提前办理的事项在客人抵店前完成。酒店已有小程序、官方App或安全的预登记页面时，可以向符合条件的住客发送入口，让本人确认订单、预计抵店时间和必要的住宿需求；系统支持且符合适用要求时，还可提前完成相应资料填写、支付或担保手续。团方统一承担的费用不要再次向个人收取，暂不能在线完成的事项则明确留待到店处理。

这些功能不是概念性的设想。Hilton官方数字入住说明包括通过App选择抵店时间、在可用条件下选房及核对付款信息；Oracle的预登记说明也支持客人在抵店前更新联系资料和预计抵店时间。不同酒店的小程序未必具备同样能力，应以实际可用功能设计流程，不能把一个收集信息的表单宣传成已经办妥入住。

On-the-way check-in可作为在途预登记的安排：客人从机场、车站前往酒店时，通过官方入口补齐未完成信息、更新预计抵店时间。整团乘车时，领队可向酒店确认车辆出发、预计抵达时间及人数变化；涉及个人资料和支付的步骤仍由住客本人在适当渠道完成，不交给领队在群内集中收集。

前厅应在客人抵店前查看提交结果，确认信息是否已经进入正确订单，哪些事项完成、哪些仍待核对，再把最新抵店时间提供给客房负责人安排交房顺序。没有系统接口的酒店，可以由授权人员核对录入，但要明确负责人及完成时点，避免客人手机上填了一遍，到店还被要求无差别重填。

这里应分清“已提交”“酒店已核对”和“房间已准备好”三种状态。小程序显示提交成功，不等于酒店确认，也不等于客人可以直接进房。只有实际完成所需核验、结算及房间交付条件，才进入领卡或适用的数字钥匙流程；能否免去柜台环节，取决于当地要求、酒店系统与该笔订单资格，不能一概承诺。

例如，可在接待前约定：团队车辆出发后更新一次预计抵店时间；前厅据此复核预登记和房态，提前联系仍有缺项的住客。客人抵店后，已核对的信息直接供柜台使用，只补办尚未完成的事项。不方便使用手机、网络不畅或预登记失败的客人，保留人工办理通道；提前办理是减少重复工作的选择，不能成为入住的新门槛。

## 正常办理与异常处理分开，但不能把客人晾在一旁

团队抵店后，可由一名熟悉名单的人员先做引导，确认客人属于哪个团队、哪一批次，并查看其预登记处理状态，再进入所需核验和入住办理，避免把已经核对的事项重新做一遍。引导的作用是减少排错队和重复询问，不是让客人先多办一道手续。

临时换房、名单不符、付款争议或证件问题，应交给明确的负责人跟进，避免正常柜台停下来等待多方确认。异常分流必须有交接：谁接手、缺什么、下一步怎么处理、何时再向客人说明。只是请客人到旁边等候，没有人负责，并没有改善接待。

已经完成手续但仍需等房的客人，应有单独的信息更新安排。值班经理根据实际条件协调行李寄存、休息区域和可兑现的交房次序；房态没有确认前，不给客人一个无法保证的领卡时间。老年人、携幼家庭或有特殊需要的客人，可以由现场负责人协调照顾，同时向其他客人说明安排，避免不透明的插队引起新的不满。

团队专用柜台也不是固定答案。人数少、到店分散时，共用柜台配合预先核对可能更合适；集中抵店时，则应保留散客办理能力。调走熟练人员后，如果另一条队伍明显变长，只是把等待转移了位置。

## 一张能直接用于准备会的核对表

酒店可以在现有工作表中设置以下栏目：团队及批次、预计抵店时间、人数与房型、名单版本、预登记提交及酒店核对状态、到店待办事项、可交付房间及待房数量、结算安排、未决事项、责任人、完成或更新时间。按批次填写，具体房号及住客信息放在受权限控制的明细中。

这张表由前厅经理汇总。销售负责抵店信息与团方变更，前厅指定人员处理线上预登记及在途更新，客房负责人更新交房状态，财务确认结算口径，值班经理处理超出现场授权的例外。抵店前由各责任人逐项确认；到店时间、名单或房态发生实质变化时，更新相关项，而不是等下一次例会。

可以用一个假设场景检验它是否有用：某团队的房间已经足够，但部分客人的押金承担方式尚未确认。这时应在抵店前解决结算口径，未解决者由指定人员跟进。如果付款信息齐全，却有一批房间未完成清洁检查，优先事项就变成协调交房顺序及等候安排。两种情形不能都用“多安排一个前台”处理。

每项未决事项都应有明确的结束条件。例如，结算问题以取得有权限人员确认、并让柜台能够查到为结束；待房问题以完成清洁检查并同步房态为结束。发出一条催办消息，不等于问题已经解决。

## 用下一批团队验证，而不是先承诺几分钟入住

先选择一批已经确认、规模可控的团队试用。记录客人进入接待等候、开始办理、手续完成及实际可入住的时间，分别观察办理前等待、办理耗时和手续完成后的等房时间；同时记录名单返工、换房、结算差错和异常处理结果。对预登记还要看已提交的信息有多少在到店时被直接使用、哪些仍需重复填写，以及客人在线办理是否遇到困难；提交率高而柜台返工未减少，就应检查信息衔接，不能只把线上办理人数当成成效。

比较时应尽量选择人数、房间准备程度和抵店集中程度相近的团队。当天客人更少、房间更早准备好，本身就可能缩短等待，不能把全部改善都归功于新流程。除了平均时间，还应看等待最长的客人卡在哪里，以及散客是否受到了影响。

如果出现错发房卡、身份核验遗漏、未清洁房间放行，或异常客人无人跟进，应立即停止有问题的批量环节，恢复逐项核对后再调整。不能用排队变短抵消交付差错。

团队入住是否顺畅，最终取决于客人抵店前有多少不确定事项已经解决，以及抵店后剩下的问题能否被及时接住。前厅经理可以从下一批团队开始，把准备表中每一个“待确认”交到具体责任人手里，再决定柜台和人手怎样安排。
contentEn:
Hotel Group Arrivals: How Can Check-in Be Organised to Reduce Queues?

To reduce queues when hotel groups arrive together, use a mini program or another suitable channel for eligible preregistration, reconcile arrival batches, rooming lists, rooms ready for occupancy and payment arrangements, and assign exceptions to a named person. More reception staff cannot shorten a wait caused by rooms that are not ready.

Group preparation requires more than a room count. The arrival times held by sales, the cleaning schedule held by housekeeping and the keys reception plans to issue must refer to the same guests. Otherwise, apparently complete arrangements still leave staff searching names, finding rooms and asking who pays the deposit after guests arrive.

Exhibition changeovers and conference registration periods warrant advance checks. The Ministry of Commerce's schedule for the 140th Canton Fair places its second phase on 23–27 October 2026. This is a planning reminder, not evidence that every nearby hotel has group arrivals. Staffing should follow confirmed bookings and arrival information, rather than converting exhibition size into assumed demand for the property.

## Establish whether guests are waiting for processing or for rooms

Guests waiting in the lobby may face two different problems. Some have rooms available but cannot finish check-in because names have changed, payment arrangements are unclear or reservations must be located repeatedly. Others have completed the formalities but their rooms still need cleaning, inspection or release from maintenance.

The first problem calls for less verification and rework at the desk. The second requires coordination of room release, waiting arrangements and communication. Combining both waits can lead reception to assume it needs another desk while housekeeping assumes guests have not completed check-in.

Preparation should compare expected arrivals with rooms genuinely ready for those arrivals. Assigning a room number is a plan; readiness for occupancy is a condition for issuing access. Do not release an unready room simply to mark a process complete in the system.

## Reconcile names, room status and payment before arrival

Sales or the group liaison should confirm arrival batches, numbers, room-type requirements and the group contact. A coach arriving together requires different arrangements from conference delegates arriving separately. Where timing remains uncertain, retain an estimated window and agree who updates it. Do not keep using the arrival time recorded in the original quotation through to arrival day.

Reception should reconcile the rooming list with reservations, including sharing arrangements, different arrival dates, early arrivals and extensions that affect allocation. Give each list an update time and an owner. Route changes through the person maintaining it, rather than leaving sales, the group leader and reception with different versions.

Housekeeping should identify rooms deliverable for each arrival batch, rather than only the total planned for cleaning that day. Reception needs to know which rooms are ready, which remain outstanding and when the next update will come. If key cards or packets are prepared in advance, verify the guest and room at handover and update them when the list changes.

Sales and finance should confirm which charges the group pays, which guests pay themselves, how deposits or guarantees are handled, and who approves extra rooms or upgrades. Reception should be able to retrieve the confirmed arrangement without calling again for every guest. A statement that the group settles everything must not conceal unresolved charges.

Oracle's OPERA Cloud documentation treats preregistration, room allocation and mass check-in separately. Mass check-in has prerequisites covering arrival status, payment information and room occupancy status. Faster processing therefore depends on preparation; selecting several reservations does not resolve every issue. Functions vary with system version and configuration, and adopting this method does not require replacing the hotel's system first.

Preparation does not establish that identity verification is complete. Article 6 of China's Measures for the Administration of Public Security in the Hotel Industry requires identity documents to be checked and information registered accurately when registering accommodation. A list supplied by the group leader does not replace the required checks and registration; procedures must also follow current local requirements. Keep only coordination information in the preparation sheet, rather than copying identity document numbers into broadly accessible work chats or public displays.

## Extend Pre-check-in to the journey to the hotel

Pre-check-in moves suitable tasks to the period before arrival. Where the hotel has a mini program, official app or secure preregistration page, send eligible guests an entry point to confirm their reservation, estimated arrival time and necessary accommodation requirements. Where the system and applicable requirements permit, guests may also complete relevant information, payment or guarantee steps in advance. Do not charge individuals again for costs covered by the group, and clearly identify tasks that must wait until arrival.

These functions already exist in practice. Hilton's official digital check-in guidance covers selecting an arrival time through its app, choosing a room where available and reviewing payment information. Oracle's preregistration guidance also supports updating contact information and estimated arrival time before arrival. A hotel's mini program may not offer the same capabilities. Design around functions actually available, and do not describe an information collection form as completed check-in.

On-the-way check-in can be organised as preregistration during the journey: guests travelling from the airport or station use an official channel to complete missing information and update their estimated arrival time. For a coach group, the leader can confirm departure, expected arrival and changes in numbers. Personal information and payment steps should still be completed by each guest through an appropriate channel, rather than collected by the leader in a group chat.

Before arrival, reception should review submissions, establish that information has reached the correct reservation, distinguish completed tasks from outstanding checks, and pass updated arrival times to housekeeping for room-release planning. Without a system interface, authorised staff can reconcile and enter information, but responsibility and timing must be clear. Guests should not fill in information on their phones only to repeat it indiscriminately at the desk.

Distinguish three statuses: submitted, checked by the hotel, and room ready. Successful submission in a mini program is neither hotel confirmation nor permission to enter the room. Move to key collection or an eligible digital-key process only after the required verification, settlement arrangements and room-release conditions have been met. Whether a guest can bypass the desk depends on local requirements, the hotel's system and reservation eligibility; do not promise it universally.

For example, agree that the group's estimated arrival time will be updated after the coach leaves. Reception can then review preregistration and room readiness, contacting guests with outstanding items in advance. On arrival, staff use information already checked and complete only outstanding tasks. Retain assisted check-in for guests who cannot conveniently use a phone, have connectivity problems or encounter failed preregistration. Advance processing should reduce duplication without becoming a new barrier to accommodation.

## Separate routine processing from exceptions while keeping ownership clear

When the group arrives, a person familiar with the list can direct guests to the correct group and batch, check preregistration status and route them to the required verification and check-in steps. Avoid repeating tasks already checked. Guidance should reduce wrong queues and repeated questions rather than add another formality.

Room changes, names that do not match, payment disputes and identity document issues need a named owner so routine desks do not stop while several parties are contacted. Every exception needs a handover: who takes it, what is missing, what happens next and when the guest will receive another update. Asking someone to wait aside without assigning responsibility does not improve reception.

Guests who have completed formalities but still await a room need a separate update arrangement. The duty manager should coordinate luggage storage, rest areas and a deliverable room-release order within actual conditions. Do not promise a key-collection time before room status is confirmed. The person in charge can coordinate assistance for older guests, families with young children and guests with particular needs, explaining arrangements to others to avoid resentment about unexplained queue-jumping.

A dedicated group desk is not always the answer. Small groups arriving separately may be better served through shared desks and advance reconciliation. For concentrated arrivals, retain capacity for other guests. Moving experienced staff merely transfers the queue if the other line becomes substantially longer.

## A preparation sheet for the arrival briefing

An existing worksheet can contain these fields: group and arrival batch, estimated arrival time, numbers and room types, list version, preregistration submission and hotel review status, outstanding arrival tasks, ready rooms and rooms still awaited, payment arrangements, unresolved items, responsible person, and completion or update time. Complete it by batch; keep individual room numbers and guest information in access-controlled detail.

The front office manager consolidates the sheet. Sales owns arrival information and group changes; a designated reception colleague handles online preregistration and journey updates; housekeeping updates room release; finance confirms payment arrangements; and the duty manager handles exceptions beyond frontline authority. Each owner confirms their items before arrival. Update affected items when timing, lists or room status change materially, rather than waiting for another meeting.

A hypothetical example tests its usefulness. Rooms are available for a group, but some guests' deposit arrangements remain unresolved. The priority is to settle the payment arrangements before arrival, with outstanding cases assigned to a person. If payment information is complete but rooms still need cleaning and inspection, the priority becomes room-release sequencing and waiting arrangements. Another receptionist is not the universal answer to both situations.

Every unresolved item needs a completion condition. A payment issue ends when an authorised person has confirmed the arrangement and the desk can retrieve it. A room wait ends when cleaning and inspection are complete and room status is updated. Sending a reminder does not close the issue.

## Test with the next group before promising check-in within minutes

Select a confirmed group of manageable size. Record when guests enter the reception queue, when processing begins, when formalities finish and when they can actually occupy their rooms. Observe pre-processing waits, processing time and subsequent room waits separately, alongside list rework, room changes, settlement errors and exception outcomes. For preregistration, also examine how much submitted information is used directly on arrival, what must be entered again and whether guests encounter difficulties online. If submission is high but desk rework remains, investigate the information handover rather than treating online participation alone as success.

Compare groups with reasonably similar numbers, room readiness and concentration of arrivals. Fewer guests or rooms ready earlier can themselves shorten queues; do not attribute all improvement to the new process. Alongside averages, examine where the longest-waiting guests became stuck and whether other guests were affected.

If keys are issued incorrectly, identity checks are missed, unclean rooms are released or exceptions have no owner, stop the affected batch-processing step and restore individual checks before adjusting it. A shorter queue does not compensate for delivery errors.

A smooth group arrival depends on how much uncertainty has been resolved beforehand and whether remaining issues receive prompt attention. For the next group, the front office manager can assign every outstanding item on the preparation sheet to a named person, then decide how to organise desks and staffing.
author: 迈创兄弟C&T
